faqs.q: What is the Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar (part code A125) used for?
faqs.a: The Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar is a textile-reinforced hose with an NBR tube and an NBR/SBR cover, for mineral oil and air lines up to 20 bar. The tube is black and non-conductive, and the hose is listed in 6 to 25 mm bores.

faqs.q: Which bore of the Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar suits my line?
faqs.a: Choose the inside diameter from 6, 8, 10, 13, 16, 19 or 25 mm to match the flow and the fitting, because the pressure rating is the same at every size. Match the outside diameter on the size table when you pick clamps, ferrules or hose guards.

faqs.q: What is the working pressure and burst pressure of the Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar?
faqs.a: Maximum working pressure is 20 bar and minimum burst pressure is 60 bar, with a 3:1 safety factor. The working pressure is the same at every listed size. Keep operating pressure at or below 20 bar, and do not read the burst figure as a working limit.

faqs.q: What are the tube, reinforcement and cover of the Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar?
faqs.a: The tube is black non-conductive NBR. The reinforcement is high tensile strength textile plies. The cover is black smooth extruded, oil, abrasion, ozone and weather resistant NBR/SBR. Operating temperature is -40°C to +80°C.

faqs.q: Which safety factor and standards apply to the Multi-Purpose Mineral Oil & Air Hose 20 Bar?

faqs.a: Four bores are listed: 1", 1-1/2", 2" and 3". Lengths run from 36 inch and 4 ft up to 25 ft, with sizes such as 10 ft, 12 ft, 15 ft, 20 ft and 25 ft. Bend radius rises with size, from 76.2 mm at 1" to 228.6 mm at 3".

faqs.q: How do I choose between the black CHX and the orange stripe FAB Continental chemical hose assemblies?
faqs.a: Both families cover the same four bores and lengths. The FAB version carries an orange stripe, which is a marking you can use to separate lines. Pick on the chemical, bore, length and fitting combination.

faqs.q: What working pressure do Continental chemical hose assemblies have?
faqs.a: The pressure is not one figure: the working pressure is given per size in the size table, and it is the maximum for continuous duty. Burst pressure is a test figure, not a working limit. Quote the part number or the bore, length and chemical, and we confirm the rating before supply.

faqs.q: What are the end fittings and chemical limits of Continental chemical hose assemblies?
faqs.a: The end fittings are Grade 316 stainless steel on both ends, and the assembly has a static control wire. Not recommended chemicals are liquid ammonia, anhydrous ammonia, methyl chloride, turpentine and xylene. Check the chemical against the hose before ordering.

faqs.q: Which safety rules apply to a Continental chemical hose assembly?
faqs.a: Select the hose on working pressure, bore, temperature and fluid, and use only end fittings from the series the hose maker approves for that hose. The static control wire dissipates static, so keep the assembly bonded to the tank or earth. See [chemical transfer hose selection](/blog/chemical-transfer-hose-selection).

faqs.q: What do I connect to a Continental chemical hose assembly?
faqs.a: The assemblies are supplied coupled, with the fittings already attached, so connect the stainless fitting to the matching thread or flange on your pump, tank or hose reel. Quote the end-fitting letters, such as CE, CC or NN, when you reorder.

faqs.q: How do I handle and store a Continental chemical hose assembly?
faqs.a: Never bend the assembly tighter than its minimum bend radius, from 76.2 mm on the 1" size to 228.6 mm on the 3" size, and do not kink or drag it. Drain and flush it after use, and keep it bonded when a chemical is flowing.
